correctness.rationale: Differentiating the exact radial-graph area element contributes 2 phi, while moving level circles contribute s delta(t-s) and -(s+h) delta(t-s-h). Funk--Hecke with standard surface measure gives 2*pi times [2 integral P_l+sP_l(s)-(s+h)P_l(s+h)], which equals the stated J_l by integration by parts. The Legendre polynomial leading coefficient is nonzero; for l>=2 the coefficient of s^l in J_l is h(1-l)c_l, proving exact degree and only finitely many exceptional offsets per degree. Harmonic orthogonality gives the full kernel. Parity proves all odd degrees invisible in centered slabs. Exact symbolic checks through l=12 and independent direct-area finite-difference checks for l=0..4 verified normalizations without substituting finite checks for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original October 1 source announces nonlinear sphere rigidity for the entire fixed-width slab family, not a linearized, single-absolute-offset inversion statement in its accessible abstract. A full later coauthored 15-page primary manuscript proves even stronger nonlinear rigidity using height densities and Newtonian averaging, but contains no Legendre or first-variation computation and no one-offset kernel classification. Semantic searches for the source, harmonic formula, equivalent radial Radon-data formulation, single-offset injection, and centered parity failure yielded no covering statement; no matching covered claim was located in the checked published scientific records. The inaccessible earlier full preprint is a genuine residual risk, explicitly recorded; the available stronger full text permits the comparison to proceed without pretending its noncoverage is certain.
residual_risks: The complete 1 October 2026 preprint could not be lawfully fetched for full-text inspection. It might contain a comparable linearization even though the later stronger coauthored paper does not.

value.rationale: The recent fixed-width Archimedean problem is a canonical sphere-characterization question involving a continuum of parallel slabs. The new theorem resolves the structurally different and natural inverse-data question: how much of that continuum is needed *infinitesimally* near a sphere? It gives a complete harmonic kernel for every offset, shows that the whole angular scan of a single generic slab location detects all shape modes up to unavoidable translations, and identifies the centered location as an infinite-dimensional blind spot. This exact measurement-design distinction and the at-most-l exceptional-root bound have mathematical utility independent of any unproved nonlinear or stability extension.
